summary: The Gobkit boar matches the brief and is within budget with no visible holes, but the 'Old Bone close before correction' assertion fails (26.0 > 20): the source's near-white eye rings and tusks were repainted to Old Bone, which looks intended but is a call for the user.

findings.observation: The source's pale group (median #E4E0D4, 6% of the UV footprint) is 26.0 dE from Old Bone #CCB484, over the 20 limit. Correction repainted it to Old Bone exactly; in the views this group is the eye-ring whites and the tusks, which now read as pale yellowed beige, plausible for tusks and eye whites. Whether to accept it is the user's call.
findings.evidence: assertion 'palette color Old Bone close before correction'; metrics.color_vs_palette; 01_front.png, 02_right.png

findings.observation: Source scale is very large for a boar: about 3.2 x 4.6 x 3.5 m at source_scale 1.0; only matters if used in the game.
A small extra hair tuft on top of the head the prompt doesn't mention; harmless.

escalation_reason: The only failing assertion is Old Bone's distance before correction (26.0 vs 20); the near-white eye rings and tusks were plausibly meant to become bone-coloured and look right. No refine or reroll applies to a sourced CC0 mesh. The user decides whether to accept the repaint or exempt this sourced asset from the check.
questions_answered: All prompt elements present (round brown body, four stub legs, big head, snout, two tusks, pointed ears, small tail), plus eye rings and a head tuft.
Nothing malformed: 12 loops over 17 parts, at most 1 per part, none visible.
Budget passes: 380 of 1320 tris, one 128 px texture; source is ~3.2 x 4.6 x 3.5 m.
Saddle Leather, Barrow Oak and Peat Black pass; Old Bone fails before (26.0) and passes after (0.0).
Not a humanoid: validate reports humanoid_mappable false, expected for a 16-bone quadruped imported as a prop; validate passes.
